title: Playing German music for the brewery crowd
summary: They played German pieces for a German society, where Mello recalls the food, until the war ended it.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: any of those Germans in? Yeah, we played German music. We used to play for the Toine Verand. Toine his heart. That was all German music. Deiz Lene Aries Augustine ! Alley, Harlow, Rosser Schimmel Schmoll, all kind of German pieces. I used to do them doito. They used to have fine liver sausage. And also they had limboiga cheese. They had two kinds of bread. had what they called black bread. And they had French loaf. But when I come in and see the whole stuff packed on the table I get myself a liver sausage and get a knife. And get my bread. And go up on the bandstand. That was on Friday. And that time I could speak jointly. And that was mostly all of the brewmasters and the breweries used to be tagging up in that house. What's good you calling that? I says, yeah. I says, you ain't cutting none of that privy cheese. I says, it'll give me something to eat on my liver. I says, uh-uh. I told him, I says, I told him a gentleman. I says, well, I says, if you care, too, I says, you eat that stuff. I said, you go to Beckhurst. I went to privy. Better known as the toilet. I says, you eat it. I said, you don't know whether you're getting that or you're getting this limbo of your cheese on your hand. And they used to laugh. They used to laugh to beat the band. We played for them a long time, too, until the war. And the war broke it up.
